beats.headline: Imani, Yolanda, the Andrews brothers, and Agatha
beats.text: Carl and Donut find them on the first floor. Tales are exchanged, plans are formed, and the Royal Court agrees to keep helping them.

beats.headline: The Ball of Swine
beats.text: Brandon, Chris, Yolanda, Imani, Carl and Donut take it down out of the redoubt. Agatha is in the room for it, bleeding from the head and doing nothing, which still counts for experience.

beats.headline: Twenty-four stayed to sing
beats.text: Only six more residents come down from the Waffle House; twenty-four vote to stay and were singing when Brandon last saw them. The rest fill the French storm shelter. The plan is to send every resident down to the third floor early, since they cannot train, and the four staff are going with them rather than risk being split up. Brandon's boss box gives him a magic boomerang; Imani does not say what she gets. Then Chris, speaking for the second time, notices Agatha was edited out of their recap.

beats.headline: Jack, Yolanda, Randall
beats.text: One resident, who had had the rule explained to him, stands up on the train and relieves himself on the dungeon wall. Yolanda Martinez puts an arrow in his temple, too late to matter, and the rage elemental that rises out of the stain cuts through her and through Randall, thrown off the last car. A hundred feet away, Chris and Imani pull the others off their seats and throw them through a safe room door. Three are dead, and the train stays outside.

beats.headline: Thirty-six go down
beats.text: Forty minutes after the elemental dies, what is left of Meadow Lark follows the scorched trail to the stairwell: thirty-six residents in three shopping-cart contraptions built from Chopper wheels and hunks of wood. Chris and Imani push the two big people buckets; Brandon pushes six. Brandon hugs Carl goodbye. Imani is the last one down the ramp, and she waves, unsmiling. Donut asks whether they will see them again. Carl does not know.

beats.headline: Selection is slow going
beats.text: Brandon's message: selection is slow going. None of the residents can choose human without staying in their current condition, and there is pushback; those with cognitive issues have to pick some really weird races to stay viable. Brandon stayed human. Chris and Imani did not. Most residents are still level one, and for reaching the third floor without killing anything or dealing damage they are getting Legendary Pacifist Boxes, among a ton of others. Some may soon be more powerful than Imani. Mistress Tiatha thinks they are far from Carl.

beats.headline: Down the ghoul coaster to Trainyard D
beats.text: They ride the conveyor all the way to Trainyard D, where the gate is breached, and land in a yard full of ghouls. A running fight carries them to the Iron Tangle's administrative building outside the yard. Elle floats above the horde and freezes them by the hundreds until everything around the building is dead, then complains to Carl for five minutes about how little experience it paid. The ghouls that arrive afterwards ignore the building and walk straight back into the tunnels. Carl suggests the employee tunnel, on foot, to the nearest transfer station.

beats.headline: A cannon full of oil
beats.text: Word reaches Carl through the chat. Meadow Lark are down to the last castle in their bubble, and it is an air castle. The plan is a cannon that shoots oil into the sky, which will hopefully bring it down. If that does not work, Elle is going to use her new Graupel spell to crash the thing. Elsewhere Li Jun and Li Na's team are about to storm an underwater castle, the last in theirs.
